layout_evidence.identity_boundary: The mNameKey ResourceKey is not used to resolve the numeric property_id. The local map key and the parent list remain separate lookup identities.

mechanics.lookup: Read the map span at list+0x18 and list+0x1c and the lookup mode at list+0x2c, then call the shared 24-byte-entry lower-bound helper 0x00612db0. The helper count is the byte distance between entries_begin and entries_end divided by 0x18 before its binary search.
mechanics.hit: Return true when the lower-bound result is not entries_end and property_id is not less than the entry key at offset 0.
mechanics.miss: On a lower-bound miss, if parent is non-null, tail-dispatch through the parent vtable slot +0x1c with the original property_id. The parent port is a one-stack-word __thiscall boundary: ECX is the parent receiver, property_id is at ESP+0x04, and the callee cleans 4 bytes. If parent is null, return false.
mechanics.sentinel: The end pointer is the map's entries_end. No ResourceKey conversion, property materialization, or cache lookup occurs.

evidence.observation: The body performs the shared lower-bound lookup, returns true on an exact map key, and otherwise dispatches to the parent or returns false.
The assembly proves map offsets +0x18/+0x1c/+0x2c, the helper's byte-distance/0x18 count, end-sentinel rejection, the one-word thiscall parent port at +0x1c, and RET 0x4.
The only direct named callee is the shared lower-bound helper at 0x00612db0.
The function has one direct call xref and one data xref.
The live type is 56 bytes with the map at +0x18 and parent at +0x30.
The conceptual key is a distinct 12-byte value at list+0x08.

unresolved_questions: Concrete parent PropertyList subtype and vtable +0x1c implementation
Whether any callers depend on property map lookup_mode values not visible in the binary search helper
blockers: The parent virtual dispatch is an opaque runtime boundary in the staging model.
No original runtime trace validates inherited property visibility.
